article.headline: Fastenal Rises 3.5% To Edge Of Record As Sales Keep Climbing
article.deck: Three sessions past a 53.02 buy point from a 12-week flat base, Fastenal trades inside its buy range, which runs to 55.67.
body: Fastenal rose 1.88, or 3.5%, to 54.87 as of 1:11 p.m. Mountain. The industrial supplier broke out Nov. 4 from a 12-week flat base that corrected 10.6%, clearing the 53.02 buy point on 1.48x its 50-day average volume. Today's gain puts it 3.5% past the buy point and inside the buy range, which tops out at 55.67. Volume is on pace for 0.59x its 50-day average.

The stock sits 0.2% below its 52-week high of 54.96. It is 8.1% above its 50-day line at 50.75 and 0.91 ATRs from the 21-day line at 52.23, so it is moving up without being stretched. Its RS line is at a new high, and it ranks 76 of 99 on the desk's list. Fastenal is up 36.7% this year and 34.6% over 12 months.

The September quarter brought EPS of 0.35, up 20.7% from a year earlier, on revenue of $2.46 billion, up 15.5%. Both lines have risen every quarter in the table: EPS from 0.26 to 0.30, 0.33 and 0.35, revenue from $2.03 billion to $2.46 billion. The market cap is about $63.0 billion at 38.9 times forward earnings. The next report is due Jan. 19.

The group is moving with it. A Nov. 4 Investor's Business Daily headline said rival Grainger surged on its best revenue growth in five years, and Grainger also broke out this week. A 24/7 Wall St. piece Monday noted Fastenal's 35% gain in 2026.
A close back under 53.02 would turn this into a stalled breakout.
article.watch: Watch the top of the buy range at 55.67 and the 52-week high at 54.96; a close above 55.67 puts the stock past the buy range.

article.headline: Tesla Jumps 6% Despite Plan To Return Cybertruck Deposits
article.deck: Tesla is a stalled breakout 1.7% under its 386.93 buy point, bouncing off the 50-day line; the buy range runs to 406.28.
body: Tesla gained 22.23, or 6.2%, to 380.45 as of 1:11 p.m. Mountain, bouncing off its 50-day line. It broke out Oct. 26 past a 386.93 buy point from a four-week flat base that corrected 10.6%, on 1.42x average volume, then slipped back under it. Ten sessions after the breakout it sits 1.7% below the buy point, a stalled breakout. Volume is on pace for 0.66x its 50-day average.

The flat base formed after a bigger correction: the stock is still 23.7% below its 52-week high of 498.83 from Dec. 22, 2025, after a fall to 297.38 on July 29. It trades 2.1% above the 50-day line at 372.77, 0.8% below the 200-day at 383.52 and flat to the 21-day line at 379.68, with an ATR reading of 0.0. Its RS line sits 30.2% below its high, and it ranks 52 of 99 on the desk's list. The stock is down 15.4% this year.

The fundamentals are weak. September-quarter EPS fell 43.6% to 0.22, and revenue slipped 0.2% to $28.05 billion. The stock carries a $1.50 trillion market cap at 176.2 times forward earnings. The next report is due Jan. 27.

The news Monday was about the Cybertruck. Musk said Tesla is on the hook for Cybertruck deposits after a cancellation, and the company plans to return deposits for many Cybertruck buyers. A 24/7 Wall St. headline noted the stock rose despite the refund warning.
A close back above 386.93 would put the breakout back on; a drop under 372.77 would undo the bounce.
article.watch: Watch whether Tesla can close back above the 386.93 buy point or holds the 50-day line at 372.77.

article.headline: BlackRock Rises 3.9% As Crypto ETF Conversions Run Into Billions
article.deck: BlackRock is 0.4% past a 1,220.04 buy point from a 53-week cup and inside its buy range, which runs to 1,281.04.
body: BlackRock rose 46.49, or 3.9%, to 1,225.36 as of 1:11 p.m. Mountain. The asset manager broke out Nov. 4 past a 1,220.04 buy point from a 53-week cup that corrected 24.8%, on 1.77x its 50-day average volume. The cup's left side peaked Oct. 15, 2025, and the low came March 12. Three sessions after the breakout, the stock is 0.4% past the buy point and well inside the buy range, which runs to 1,281.04. Volume is on pace for 0.67x its 50-day average.

It trades 1.3% below its 52-week high of 1,242.12. The stock is 10.8% above its 50-day line at 1,106.13 and 1.21 ATRs from the 21-day line at 1,151.05, so the trend is intact without being stretched. The RS line sits 3.4% below its high, and BlackRock ranks 72 of 99 on the desk's list. It is up 14.5% this year.

September-quarter EPS rose 25.4% to 10.57, and revenue grew 19.1% to $7.75 billion. Quarterly EPS has moved unevenly across the table, from 7.16 to 14.06, 12.19 and 10.57, while revenue climbed from $6.70 billion in the March quarter to $7.75 billion. The market cap is about $189.3 billion at 18.9 times forward earnings. The next report is due Jan. 14.
Barron's reported that BlackRock is seeing billions in crypto ETF conversions, driven by security fears. Separate headlines said bitcoin ETFs saw $1.28 billion in outflows.
A close back under 1,220.04 would make this a stalled breakout.
article.watch: Watch the 1,220.04 buy point as support and the 52-week high at 1,242.12 overhead.
